# The Engine vs Frameworks comparisons stop sending business-app teams back to React, Vue and Angular

## Context

The operator asked for the release-blocking front-door read: where do our pages undersell Neo for no reason, and where do they directly or indirectly push the target audience away? `learn/benefits/Introduction.md` is the positive bar. That read covered `learn/README.md` and `learn/benefits/body/*` (#20518 / PR #20519), the root README (#20538) and the multi-window and features pages (#20539 / PR #20542). The Engine vs Frameworks section (`learn/comparisons/`) is where an evaluator decides, and it is not yet covered. Read at `dev` `b0e5fceb91`, five of its six pages close by telling the reader when to stay with the other tool.

## The Problem

- **The conclusions send the core audience away.** `NeoVsVue.md:85`: *"For many websites and standard business applications, Vue's performance and developer experience are best-in-class for the main-thread paradigm. It is an exceptional tool."* `:87` follows with: *"Neo.mjs offers a different solution for a different class of problems."* `NeoVsReact.md:174`: React *"remains a viable choice"* for teams *"heavily invested in the React ecosystem"*, and Neo is for apps where performance is *"critical"*. `NeoVsAngular.md:101`: Angular *"remains a robust choice"* for teams invested in it. `NeoVsSolid.md:78`: *"Solid.js for ultimate Main Thread rendering speed"*. `NeoVsNextJs.md:119-120`: Next.js is *"an excellent solution"* for content-rich pages. Standard business applications are exactly the audience a complete application platform is built for.
- **The ecosystem bullets concede without the counterpoint.** `NeoVsReact.md:163`, `NeoVsVue.md:80`, `NeoVsAngular.md:90` and `NeoVsSolid.md:69` each end with *"Neo.mjs has a smaller but dedicated community"*. None says why the comparison is uneven: those libraries ship a view layer and leave grids, forms, docking, state and routing to third-party packages, while Neo.mjs ships them in one install (more than 450 classes, maintained together).
- **`NeoVsNextJs.md` gates and undersells.** The §2 heading is *"Neo.mjs: Complex, Interactive SPAs & Enterprise Applications"*. The trade-off table says *"SEO: Requires pre-rendering solution"*, yet the engine hydrates server-rendered markup (`useSSR`, `src/Main.mjs:530`, `src/worker/Manager.mjs:300`). "Next.js as a Content Shell" routes landing pages and blog posts away by default, while neomjs.com's own portal, docs and blog run on Neo.mjs (`apps/portal`).
- **`Overview.md:18` hedges:** *"When Neo.mjs **might** be the optimal choice."*

## The Fix

Rewrite each conclusion so it positions Neo.mjs for the same applications those teams build today, from everyday business apps to data-heavy multi-window workspaces, and so it states what Neo adds: the batteries, zero-build development, off-main-thread runtime, multi-window and the Neural Link. Stay respectful of the other library, without flattering it into the default. Give each ecosystem bullet its honest counterpoint (keep the community-size fact). Fix the Next.js heading, the SEO row and the content-shell framing. Drop the Overview hedge. Leave the technical comparison tables alone.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] **AC-1:** No comparison conclusion tells a reader to stay with React, Vue, Angular or Solid for ordinary applications. Each names the applications Neo.mjs builds (business apps included) and what it adds.
- [ ] **AC-2:** Each "Ecosystem & Maturity" bullet keeps the community-size fact and adds the batteries counterpoint.
- [ ] **AC-3:** `NeoVsNextJs.md`'s use-case heading covers interactive applications of every size, its SEO row states the engine's SSR hydration accurately, and the content-shell section no longer routes content sites away by default.
- [ ] **AC-4:** `Overview.md:18`'s hedge is gone. `check-relative-links.mjs` and `check-whitespace.mjs` pass.

## Out of Scope

- The comparison tables' technical rows (worker model, reactivity, rendering), unless a row is factually stale.
- `NeoVsExtJs.md`, which already closes as "a compelling and technically superior successor to Ext.js".
- New comparison pages.

## Avoided Traps

- **Trashing the other libraries.** Respect stays; the fix removes the invitation to leave, not the fairness.
- **Claiming SSR is built in end to end.** The engine hydrates server-rendered output; the server renderer lives outside this repository, so the row says exactly that.
